detail.longDescription: Anthropic Just Completed the Biggest IPO in History Anthropic just completed the largest IPO in history, and the market did not blink. The Claude maker raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday night, then started trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT. Shares touched $114.99 in the debut session, well above the $83 offer price — a first-day pop on a deal that had already priced above its own range. Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares at $83 each, up from an initial range of $70 to $78, because demand would not let it stay there. The listing alone beats SpaceX, which raised $75 billion when it went public in June. Add $26 billion from AMD, Broadcom, Google, Microsoft and Nvidia, and the fundraising total lands near $107 billion, against a valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion. What that valuation rests on: Revenue, not profit. Anthropic booked nearly $17 billion in the third quarter, up 45% from the previous one, and has still not turned a profit. A very large bill. It carries $6.2 billion of debt and has committed close to a trillion dollars to chips and infrastructure through 2045. A nervous market. AI stocks have slid from their July peak, Nvidia is down more than a third since Jensen Huang's exit, and data centre projects keep meeting local resistance. That is the whole bet in one line: the first frontier lab to go public is asking investors to believe the spending turns into profit before the enthusiasm runs out. It also means Anthropic is now pricing risks its own founder keeps naming in public. In September, Dario Amodei called for an industrywide slowdown in AI development. The benchmark is set either way: every AI company still private now has a number to argue with. 📷 Clyde Charles Brown · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons 🔗 Source: CBS News 📷 Clyde Charles Brown · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons 🔗 Source: CBS News # AI # MachineLearning # LLM
